Question: How many sequences of zeros and/or ones of length \(20\) have all the zeros consecutive, or all the ones consecutive, or both?
Solution:
Method 1: Method 1: Count two overlapping families

Count sequences with a single block of zeros, then sequences with a single block of ones, correcting for sequences counted twice.

Let \(Z\) consist of sequences containing at least one zero, with all zeros consecutive. If the zero block has length \(k\), where \(1\le k\le20\), its first position has \(21-k\) possibilities. Every position outside that block must contain a one, so each placement determines exactly one sequence. Hence
\[
|Z|=20+19+\cdots+1=\frac{20\cdot21}{2}=210.
\]
Similarly, the family \(O\) containing a nonempty single block of ones has \(210\) sequences. Both constant sequences are included: the all-zero sequence belongs to \(Z\), and the all-one sequence belongs to \(O\).

A sequence in both families contains both digits, each in one block. It must therefore consist of a zero block followed by a one block, or the reverse. There are \(19\) possible boundaries and \(2\) choices for the first digit, giving \(38\) sequences in the overlap. Every requested sequence belongs to at least one family, so the required count is
\[
210+210-38=\boxed{382},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{E}\).

Method 2: Method 2: Count changes of digit

A run is a maximal consecutive block of equal digits. For example, \(0011100\) has three runs.

A sequence qualifies exactly when it has at most three runs. With one or two runs, every occurring digit occupies one block. With three runs, the middle run contains every occurrence of one digit, so that digit is consecutive. With four or more runs, alternation forces both digits to occupy at least two separate blocks, so neither is consecutive.

There are \(19\) gaps between the \(20\) positions. Choosing which gaps contain changes, together with the first digit, determines a sequence uniquely. Thus there are \(2\) sequences with one run, \(2\cdot19\) with two runs, and
\[
2\binom{19}{2}=2\cdot\frac{19\cdot18}{2}=342
\]
with three runs. The cases are disjoint and cover every qualifying sequence, giving
\[
2+38+342=\boxed{382},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
